name: All-American Beef Stew
headnote: J. Kenji Lopez-Alt sets out to rescue American beef stew from convenience, laying out thirteen rules drawn from dozens of test batches. He avoids pre-cut stew meat in favor of a whole chuck roast sliced into steaks, which he sears before cubing because cubes shed too much water and steam rather than brown, then cuts into large chunks so they stay juicy; flour stays down around two tablespoons for five cups of liquid, since more thickener dulls flavor, and body comes instead from powdered gelatin, which thickens while emulsifying the fat rather than muddying the broth. Flavor is built on chicken rather than boxed beef stock, a cup of cheap dry wine reduced down, and umami ingredients - tomato paste, anchovies, soy sauce and Worcestershire - blended smooth into the stock. Vegetables are split into two batches, large aromatics that flavor the pot and are then fished out, and browned mushrooms, carrots, pearl onions and Yukon golds added later, with the pot going into the oven lid-cracked so it holds a bare simmer without overcooking the meat.
comment_digest: The most common problem is that the stew finishes undercooked: multiple cooks report tough beef and hard potatoes past the stated time, and the fix they converge on is raising the oven to 320-325 F or finishing on the stovetop. Serious Eats has acknowledged this and bumped the published temperature from 275 F to 300 F, so older comments predate the change. Many refuse to discard the spent aromatics: blending them back in adds body without more flour, a good gluten-free thickener, though the celery goes stringy. Substitutions that work include fish sauce or anchovy paste for anchovy fillets, coconut aminos plus a Parmesan rind for the whole umami group, arrowroot for missing gelatin packets, and short ribs or venison for chuck. Several double the mushrooms and potatoes, and one advises checking the beef for tenderness before the potatoes go in. The stated five-minute prep time is widely mocked.
flags: The page carries an editor's note that the oven temperature was raised from 275 F to 300 F after reader feedback, so undercooking complaints dated before that change may no longer apply. Several comments end in 'Read More' and may be truncated.
